## What it is

- The **Minimoog Model D** is a synthesizer made by **Moog Music**, first sold in **1970** (Wikipedia, "Minimoog").
- Before it, synthesizers were big modular systems joined with patch cords. The Model D put the oscillators, filter and envelopes behind fixed switches in one box.
- The composer David Borden said it "took the synthesizer out of the studio and put it into the concert hall" (quoted in Wikipedia, "Minimoog").
- It plays **one note at a time**: it is a *monophonic* synth.

## Its sound

- It has **three oscillators** on every note, so one key can sound thick or even like a chord (Model D manual, pp. 16-19).
- Its **ladder filter** takes away high harmonics at 24 dB per octave and can whistle when Emphasis is high (manual, pp. 29-31).
- Its output can be fed back into its own mixer, which **overloads** it and makes a growl (manual, pp. 27, 36).
- Two **contours** (envelopes) shape the filter and the loudness over time (manual, pp. 30-31).

## Guided tour

Each step loads one of the manual's own patch sheets (Moog Music, *Minimoog Model D* manual, pp. 55-76) onto the panel and plays a short bass line. Open **Show the patch sheet** to see the page's drawing of that sheet.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-sheet="sub-bass"><p><b>One oscillator, one wave.</b> <i>Sub Bass</i> (p. 68) uses only Oscillator 1, on its lowest 32' range, with the soft <b>triangle</b> wave. Listen for a deep, round, plain tone.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-sheet="kraft-bass"><p><b>Three oscillators together.</b> <i>Kraft Bass</i> (p. 56) turns all three oscillators on in the <b>Mixer</b> and also the <b>External input</b> (the feedback). Listen for how much thicker and dirtier it is than step 1.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-sheet="soft-rez-bass"><p><b>Close the filter, add Emphasis.</b> <i>Soft Rez Bass</i> (p. 70) sets the <b>Cutoff</b> low and <b>Emphasis</b> to 5. Listen for a soft tone with a little "wow" ring at the start of each note.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-sheet="bubble-bass"><p><b>The filter contour.</b> <i>Bubble Bass</i> (p. 63) sets the cutoff right down and the contour <b>Amount</b> high, with a long filter decay. Listen for each note opening up and closing again: a "bubble".</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-sheet="3-square-lead"><p><b>Glide.</b> <i>3-Square Lead</i> (p. 63) uses three square waves and turns <b>Glide</b> on. Listen for the pitch sliding from one note to the next.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-sheet="singing-wind"><p><b>Noise, no oscillators.</b> <i>Singing Wind</i> (p. 71) turns every oscillator off and the <b>Noise</b> on, with high Emphasis. Listen for wind that whistles at a pitch.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-sheet="hi-hat"><p><b>A short loudness contour.</b> <i>Hi-Hat</i> (p. 59) is noise with a very short <b>loudness decay</b>. Listen: a synth can make a drum sound too.</p></div>
```

## Famous records

Named in Wikipedia, "Minimoog":

- Sun Ra, *My Brother the Wind* (1970)
- Kraftwerk, *Autobahn* (1974) and *The Man-Machine* (1978)
- Parliament, "Flash Light"

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="2"><p><b>How many oscillators does the Model D have on every note?</b></p><ul><li>One</li><li>Two</li><li>Three</li><li>Six</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Three oscillators, all on the same note (manual pp. 16-19).</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>How many notes can it play at once?</b></p><ul><li>One: it is monophonic</li><li>Five</li><li>Eight</li><li>Sixteen</li></ul><p class="ik-why">It plays one note at a time.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="1"><p><b>You turn the Cutoff knob down. What do you hear?</b></p><ul><li>Louder</li><li>Darker: fewer high harmonics</li><li>Higher pitch</li><li>An echo</li></ul><p class="ik-why">The low-pass filter takes away high harmonics.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What does Glide do?</b></p><ul><li>Slides the pitch from note to note</li><li>Adds reverb</li><li>Turns on the noise</li><li>Plays chords</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Step 5: the pitch slides.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="1"><p><b>Which year did the Model D first go on sale?</b></p><ul><li>1958</li><li>1970</li><li>1983</li><li>1999</li></ul><p class="ik-why">1970 (Wikipedia).</p></div>
```
